headline: AudioLLM interrupt-and-silent training reports proactive alerts in bounded sound benchmarks
summary: A September 18 arXiv paper proposes Interrupt and Silent Modeling (ISM), which adds <interrupt> and <silent> decisions to an audio-language model so one watch-out intent can drive continuous alerts without a new query for every event. On ESC-50, the authors report 99.6% interrupt F1 and 100.0% recall for suppressing duplicate alerts. In a zero-shot Epic-Sounds evaluation, interrupt F1 was 67.5 and onset recall 96.7%, but irrelevant-silence recall was 10.1% and sustained-relevance recall 41.2%; duplicate suppression was not measured there. The reported 3.5-second mean latency comes from 400 constructed streams with the event onset fixed at five seconds. These are author-reported benchmark results, not evidence of wearable deployment or improved outcomes for Deaf and Hard of Hearing users.
